Chinese trawlers plundering our coastline

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
It was thanks to a concerted effort of citizens action through social media which took on the massive industry of illegal fishing seeing 4 Chinese vessels detained and charged under international conventions. They alerted the local authorities to the presence of a fleet of 22 Chinese vessels illegally fishing in South African waters. 4 Chinese vessels have been detained over the last two weeks. This is the first major joint operation of the DAFF patrol vessels alongside the Navy and the SAP to apprehend illegal fishing vessels. Illegal fishing robs the South African economy of millions of rand each year and threatens jobs and food security. The 600 tons of squid caught in the closed breeding season in SA Economic Exclusion Zone the EEZ are estimated to be over R70 million to the South African economy and valuable foreign exchange

Press Release:


Illegal Fishing
Foreign trawlers illegally fishing along South Africa’s coastlines are said to cost the country upwards of R6-billion each year. For years illegal vessels have plundered the country’s marine resources, threatening fish stocks and food security. But the navy is finally cracking down and this week three Chinese trawlers were impounded in the East London harbour with a haul of 600 tons of fish and squid. Carte Blanche asks: could this signal the end of illegal fishing?


Script:


Script: Pirate fishing is an international crisis costing the global economy 350 billion rand every year. It’s wiping out fish stocks and threatening food security. Asian waters have largely been fished out so they are plundering our poorly policed waters. The Tuna and Squid stocks are being stripped.
Link: This week the normally quiet town of East London jumped into the international spotlight with citizen action becoming the first line of fire in the defence against the onslaught of illegal fishing which is happening on an industrial scale.
Script: Murray Du Plessis a passionate fishermen and member of the Border deep sea fishing association had been monitoring vessels off our coast line with an App called Marine Traffic
John “It is almost like an Ocean Neighbourhood watch, isn’t it is a bunch of concerned citizens keeping an eye on the oceans
Murry “Quite correct. There are a number of sites one can use and there is also the app. You can see the vessel direction, it’s ground speed, and then you can go and follow its past track. What really catches your attention is when you see a fleet of vessels. We saw a fleet of Chinese vessels and a much larger fleet of Taiwanese vessels and in monitoring them all of a sudden a couple of them disappeared off the VMS vessel
Script: A social media storm had been brewing for weeks with arm chair environmentalist expressing outrage at the number of vessels off our coastline. Mike Loewe local journalist on Daily Dispatch newspaper is the go to guy on ocean issues.
John “Why do you think it got so much traction on social media platforms?
Mike Loewe “Off the wild coast there has been the allegation and the fear that trawlers have been nipping in at night and just plundering our marine protected areas. …. the boarder deep sea angling association they have really been quite powerful and vocal about it and they have really been asking Government if they can we be your eyes and ears and I think this facebook moment finally brought to the fore
Script: John Rance involved for the last 30 years with Deep Sea fishing is the environmental officer for the Association and has been bombarding the authorities with evidence hoping they will take action
John Rance “In the past we have tried to establish contact and make ourselves credible to show that we were knowledgeable and the things that we were seeing, they weren’t rumours they were actual fact and we didn’t seem to get through
Mike Loewe “They have been watching our stock for chocka deplete all the time and even from natural depletion and even with our quotas it’s still getting less and less so something is wrong…. and I think that uproar finally Government listened
Script: But it’s the Wild West out there, 9 illegal vessels fled the week before with DAFF only managing to get one into Cape Town harbour. So the following Friday when two illegal Chinese vessels were spotted a joint operation was launched between the Navy, SAPs and DAFF. Initially they co-operated and switched off their engines. But the seas were too rough for officials to board, and 48 hours later without communicating their intentions, they tried to flee- it was 2am on Sunday morning
Mike Loewe “I am told the choppers were used and fisheries inspectors and naval officers were dropped on these boats and they really made quite sure they weren’t going to be embarrassed like the last time when a poor little DAFF boat had to tried to herd 9 of these vessels into Cape Town and off course they all just fled and they could only hang onto one.
Link : “After an action packed chase on the high seas 2 Chinese trawlers and an Indonesian vessel was intercepted en route, were escorted back to the harbour of East London and this is where they will stay until their fate is sealed
Script: There are over 600 tons of squid on board the 3 vessels but locals say it could be as much as 800. And although the origin of the squid is yet to be determined Dino Moodaley chair of the South African Squid Management Association says it’s extremely worrying.
Dino “If it is SA squid the value of that is close to R80 million rand because all our squid is exported and that’s foreign exchange that is coming into the country
John: For SA water in particular nobody should be fishing for squid
Dino Moodaley “We have closed the season in conjunction with DAFF for 3 months and this particular 3 months we chose is the winter spawning months and obviously with the foreign vessels coming there is a big possibility if they are catching, if they are catching in our waters they are catching our breeding stock
Script: Which happened three years back, squid boats barely set sail for two years because stocks were so depleted. It’s hardly surprising when you see the industrial scale fishing going on out there
Dino “Just the way they fish with the automated Jiggers compared to the way we in SA fish, our way of fishing is much more environmentally friendly and with them coming in with those big boats and automated jiggers they very quickly can kill a resource
Script: This is the first major operation against Illegal fishing undertaken in years. Our fish are being plundered within the 200 nautical mile economic exclusion zone, the EEZ, which is governed by the local authorities in an effort to protect fish stocks and jobs. Any fishing vessel entering the EEZ must have a permit says Advocate Nkosinati Dana Acting Chief Director of Monitoring and Surveillance
Dana ”The scientists as well as the economists have worked out the estimate of illegal fishing to around 6 billion rands per annum
John Rance “These guys are international pirates they in the super league they are up there with drug smugglers and ivory and rhino horn poaching they couldn’t give a dam for any convention the only thing they understand is when you hit them so dam hard that it is not worth them coming into your area and that is what we are going to have to do and unfortunately because we have been seen as an easy area to target in the past they will be back.They are environmental rapists.
Script: With only 4 aging patrol vessels, South Africa is woefully under equipped to patrol the 1.5 million square kilometres of ocean around our coastline
Murray “ Just of last evening we saw a fleet of 3 vessels bearing the same name travelling north east from Port Alfred towards East London and having a look early hours of this morning the vessels disappeared completely
John Rance “All commercial fishing boats have to have their AIS on all the time. The AIS is an automatic identification system which signal is monitored through the vessels monitoring system which is the VMS and the reason why they switch them off is so they can be hidden from view so when you know a commercial fishing vessel has his AIS off you must know he is up to skull duggery
John Webb “If the citizenry can see what is happening and they can upload the software to their phones and their computers and keep an eye on what is happening off our coast line why can’t DAFF do that?
John Rance “That’s a very good question, and one that disturbs us considerably. I don’t really know what facilities they have got available to them but I do know there is some really good technology in the Navy and Silvermine. The point is that any vessel going up this coast can be identified and it can be identified that they are switching their vessel monitoring system on and off that immediately should arouse suspicion. Secondly any fishing vessel entering our economic zone needs to have a permit to do so. And DAFF must surely know which ones have permits and which don’t have permits so why they couldn’t jump onto this I don’t know
Link: “It’s very clear the officials are very skittish- the harbour is in virtual lock down but it is no wonder because this has potential to balloon into a diplomatic incident
Script: Advocate Dana refused to comment on diplomatic relations with China saying this was a matter for the Minister. He could however comment on the Chinese embassy’s statement that the vessels were not violating the EEZ they were simply trying to avoid bad weather
Dana “It is the first time I have heard they were fleeing the bad weather. The requirement is that before they come into our territorial waters they should have applied for a permit to enter
Link: While the investigation unfolds more than 100 crew are stranded on board because they don’t have the correct documents
Script: China boasts the largest distant water fishing fleet, there are over 500 vessels along the African coast line alone, many of which are accused of illegal activities
John Rance “The evidence points to them coming in and going straight out to sea again. Now these vessels are fairly small, the one here I understand hasn’t been back to port for 18 months therefore they must be feeding some kind of mother vessel that is sitting outside the EEZ at 200 nautical miles where they can bunker take on food and dump their catch in decent freezing facilities otherwise how else are they operating
Script: This week we saw the power of ordinary citizens taking on the might of the massive illegal fishing scourge from of their homes
Murray “I think we should consider ourselves the first line of Defence because we are the ears and eyes on the ground and have got the vested interests in looking after the resources and if we get the kind of response like we have from DAFF and the government and these vessel are taken in I mean I think it is a tremendous job done
Mike Loewe “I think they feel empowered now by the fact that the moment they start photographing it and putting it out on Facebook and contacting journalist something happens “
Script: And although locals were encouraged by the reaction this week it’s only the tip of the iceberg, they continued to spot suspicions vessels behaving oddly throughout the week
Link: “Another sign of just how seriously this matter is being treated is that the Hawks have taken over the investigation and the Captains of the trawlers are facing 3 charges.
John Rance “ If they get a slap on the wrist and a reasonably affordable fine they will grin and bear it and head out to sea and as soon as our boats go back to Cape Town and PE they will be back there again. If you start doing what the Argentinian Navy did where apparently that boat came back in again after they were apprehended and they said off the vessel and they sank it. Really if you start doing that you will make an impact
